CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Southeast Minahasa Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the Principles of Autonomy and assistance duties with the principle of the broadest possible Autonomy in the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Southeast Minahasa. 5. Provincial Government is the Provincial Government of North Sulawesi. 6. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Southeast Minahasa Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 7. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a Regional Government Work Unit related to the implementation of child protection. 8. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the financial plan of the Region that is discussed and jointly approved by the Regional Government and DPRD and established by Regional Regulation. 9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 11. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect. 12. Special protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 13. Parent is the biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 16. Community is family, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Social Organization, hereinafter referred to as Orsos, is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community, whether legal entity or not, which functions as a means of community participation in implementing Social Welfare Efforts (UKS). 18. Child Protection Social House, hereinafter abbreviated as RSPA, is a child protection service unit for child victims of violence and child trafficking as a continuation of temporary shelter that functions to provide protection, recovery, rehabilitation, advocacy and referral. 19. Social Services for Children is physical, mental and social services aimed at helping children to grow and develop normally. 20. Social Services for Neglected Children is social services for children whose parents do not have the ability to meet the needs of children to grow and develop normally. 21. Child-friendly school is an educational institution that recognizes and respects children's rights to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, freedom to express views, and participate in making decisions according to their capacity. 22. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in implementing social welfare efforts. 23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking as well as women and children victims of violence. 24. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and formed at the Regency, District and Village levels. Article 2

The principles of protection for Victims are:

a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; and
e. empowerment. Article 3

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children; b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence. Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling of victims of violence in the Region. CHAPTER II VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence against women and children include:

a. physical violence; b. psychological violence; c. sexual violence; d. domestic neglect; e. exploitation; and
f. other violence. Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury. Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of the household and/or outside the scope of the household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

CHAPTERV PROTECTION OF VICTIMS

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization on laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

Article 11

Other violence as referred to in Article 5 letter f is caused by:

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that give rise to fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 49

(1) Any person who commits any form of violence as referred to in Article 5 shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(2) Regional Work Units that do not implement the provisions of Article 14, Article 15 and Article 16 shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) Any person who directly witnesses violence as referred to in Article 5 and does not report it to the competent authorities shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 22

(1) PPT is established by the Regional Government in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit (UPT).

(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER XI CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 50

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Southeast Minahasa Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA REGENCY NUMBER YEAR 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of fulfillment of victims' basic rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain opportunities (access), as well as welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d

What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e

What is meant by "empowerment" is strengthening victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

Article 8 Sufficiently clear.

Article 9 Sufficiently clear.

Article 10 Sufficiently clear.

Article 11 Sufficiently clear.

Article 12

Letter a

What is meant by "the right to have their dignity and worth respected as a human being" is upholding human rights.

Letter b

Sufficiently clear.

Letter c

Sufficiently clear.

Letter d

What is meant by "the right to obtain information" is the right to obtain information, statements, ideas, and signs containing value, meaning, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with developments in information and communication technology both electronically and non-electronically related to acts of violence.

Letter e

Sufficiently clear.

Letterf

What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills training.

Letter g

What is meant by "the right to social rehabilitation" includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal aid to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, and citizenship.

Letterh

What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.

Letteri

Sufficiently clear.

Letterj

What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious counselors, advocates, and family members.

Article 22

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (3)

What is meant by "safe house" is a temporary shelter intended to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence. Temporary protection is provided for a period of up to 14 (fourteen) days and can be extended according to the condition of the victim. PPT that do not have a shelter can network with PPT that have a shelter.

Paragraph (4)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (5)

Sufficiently clear.

Article 9

Domestic neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is:

a. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope whereas according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to that person.
b. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to him/her or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and
c. an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Part Three

Family

Article 21

Letter a

Prevention efforts in the family and/or closest relatives can be conducted by strengthening resilience in the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication among family members.

Letter b

Prevention efforts in the community include: cultivating environmental awareness of acts of violence occurring in their environment.

Letter c

Educational institutions can participate in efforts to provide educational punishment, seeking to abolish provisions that do not favor victims of violence.

Letter d

What is meant by "community institutions" are institutions formed by members of the community of Citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily on the basis of shared vision, mission, profession, function and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.

Article 31

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

What is meant by "other service units" is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women and children victims of violence. This service unit can be located at the Integrated Service Center (PPT) and Integrated Crisis Center (PKT) based at Hospitals, Community Health Centers, Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment (P2TP2A), Women and Children Service Unit (UPPA), Trauma Center Shelter House (RPTC), Children's Social Shelter House (RPSA), BP4, and other security institutions, prosecutors' offices, courts, Women Crisis Center (WCC), and other similar institutions. This service can be in the form of one roof (one stop crisis center) or in the form of a network, depending on the needs in each region.

Article 19 Sufficiently clear.

Article 20 Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by "network" includes: family partners, dasawisma, family groups existing in the Region.

Letter b

What is meant by "coordination" includes: planning, implementation and monitoring of violence prevention programs.

Letter c

What is meant by "violence prevention system" includes: mapping of locations or areas prone to violence and conducting promotive and preventive efforts to the community.

Letter d

Socialization can be conducted through mass media, electronic media, and direct outreach to the community.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 12

Every Victim receives the following rights: a. the right to have their dignity respected as a human being; b. the right to health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; c. the right to determine their own decisions; d. the right to obtain information; e. the right to confidentiality of identity; f. the right to compensation; g. the right to social rehabilitation; h. the right to complaint handling; i. the right to obtain facilitation in the judicial process; and j. the right to assistance.

Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intent to benefit oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or molestation.

Paragraph 2 Fulfillment of the Rights of Child Victims of Violence

Article 44

(1) Regional Government, PPT, and the community are obliged to fulfill the rights of child victims of violence.

(2) Forms of fulfillment of the rights of child victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include the fulfillment of children's basic rights in accordance with their needs.

Article 16

The Regional Government is obligated and responsible to:

a. supervise the provision of services to victims of violence, with minimum service standards; and
b. provide funds for the protection of victims through the Regional Budget and/or other legitimate regional financial sources.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intent to benefit oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or molestation.

Article 15

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children; b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence. Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling of victims of violence in the Region. CHAPTER II VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence against women and children include:

a. physical violence; b. psychological violence; c. sexual violence; d. domestic neglect; e. exploitation; and
f. other violence. Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury. Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of the household and/or outside the scope of the household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Article 9

Domestic neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is:

a. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope whereas according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to that person.
b. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to him/her or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and
c. an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intent to benefit oneself or others;

a. job training;

a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of words, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether or not using means that give rise to fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

CHAPTERV PROTECTION OF VICTIMS

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization on laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 49

(1) Any person who commits any form of violence as referred to in Article 5 shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(2) Regional Work Units that do not implement the provisions of Article 14, Article 15 and Article 16 shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) Any person who directly witnesses violence as referred to in Article 5 and does not report it to the competent authorities shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Letter a

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain opportunities (access), as well as welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d

What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e

What is meant by "empowerment" is strengthening victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 22

(1) PPT is established by the Regional Government in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit (UPT).

(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 12

Every Victim receives the following rights: a. the right to have their dignity respected as a human being; b. the right to health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; c. the right to determine their own decisions; d. the right to obtain information; e. the right to confidentiality of identity; f. the right to compensation; g. the right to social rehabilitation; h. the right to complaint handling; i. the right to obtain facilitation in the judicial process; and j. the right to assistance.

Article 5

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA REGENCY NUMBER YEAR 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

CHAPTER X SANCTIONS

Article 49

(1) Any person who commits any form of violence as referred to in Article 5 shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

(2) Regional Work Units that do not implement the provisions of Article 14, Article 15 and Article 16 shall be subject to administrative sanctions.

(3) Any person who directly witnesses violence as referred to in Article 5 and does not report it to the competent authorities shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Article 23

(1) The organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 22 paragraph (1) consists of:

a. General Chairperson:
b. Secretary:
c. Treasurer; and
d. Executive Chairperson who oversees divisions.
(2) The divisions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, at a minimum include:
a. complaint service division:
b. health service division:
c. social rehabilitation service division;
d. repatriation and social reintegration division; and
e. legal aid service division.
(3) In carrying out its duties, PPT is responsible to the Regent through the Head of the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 27

The repatriation and social reintegration division as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) letter d has the duties:

a. conducting coordination with relevant agencies for the repatriation of victims;
b. making progress reports on the process of repatriation assistance and social rehabilitation; and
c. conducting monitoring for at least three months after the victim is returned to their family.

Article 37

Social rehabilitation services as referred to in Article 33 letter d are services provided by companions in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims, including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation against victims and provide social support so that victims have confidence, strength, and independence in resolving their problems, by:

a. providing spiritual guidance to victims; and
b. psychological recovery of victims.

Article 12

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

Article 12

Every Victim receives the following rights: a. the right to have their dignity respected as a human being; b. the right to health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; c. the right to determine their own decisions; d. the right to obtain information; e. the right to confidentiality of identity; f. the right to compensation; g. the right to social rehabilitation; h. the right to complaint handling; i. the right to obtain facilitation in the judicial process; and j. the right to assistance.

Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intent to benefit oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or molestation.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA REGENCY NUMBER YEAR 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

Child-friendly school is an educational institution that recognizes and respects children's rights to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, freedom to express views, and participate in making decisions according to their capacity. 22. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in implementing social welfare efforts. 23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking as well as women and children victims of violence. 24. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and formed at the Regency, District and Village levels. Article 2

The principles of protection for Victims are:

a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; and
e. empowerment. Article 3

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children; b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence. Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling of victims of violence in the Region. CHAPTER II VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence against women and children include:

a. physical violence; b. psychological violence; c. sexual violence; d. domestic neglect; e. exploitation; and
f. other violence. Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury. Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of the household and/or outside the scope of the household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Article 10

Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:

a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intent to benefit oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or molestation.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS

Article 12

Every Victim receives the following rights: a. the right to have their dignity respected as a human being; b. the right to health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim; c. the right to determine their own decisions; d. the right to obtain information; e. the right to confidentiality of identity; f. the right to compensation; g. the right to social rehabilitation; h. the right to complaint handling; i. the right to obtain facilitation in the judicial process; and j. the right to assistance.

Article 2

Letter a

What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of fulfillment of victims' basic rights.

Letter b

What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain opportunities (access), as well as welfare;

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men, including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c

What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment towards victims without making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d

What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is that all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e

What is meant by "empowerment" is strengthening victims of violence to be able to endeavor and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.

Paragraph 1 Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 40

Forms of empowerment of women victims of violence include:

a. job training;
b. productive economic business and joint business groups; and
c. capital assistance.

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

CHAPTERV PROTECTION OF VICTIMS

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization on laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

CHAPTERV PROTECTION OF VICTIMS

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization on laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 22

(1) PPT is established by the Regional Government in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit (UPT).

(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF SOUTHEAST MINAHASA REGENCY NUMBER YEAR 2016 CONCERNING PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect. 12. Special protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 13. Parent is the biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 16. Community is family, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Social Organization, hereinafter referred to as Orsos, is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community, whether legal entity or not, which functions as a means of community participation in implementing Social Welfare Efforts (UKS). 18. Child Protection Social House, hereinafter abbreviated as RSPA, is a child protection service unit for child victims of violence and child trafficking as a continuation of temporary shelter that functions to provide protection, recovery, rehabilitation, advocacy and referral. 19. Social Services for Children is physical, mental and social services aimed at helping children to grow and develop normally. 20. Social Services for Neglected Children is social services for children whose parents do not have the ability to meet the needs of children to grow and develop normally. 21. Child-friendly school is an educational institution that recognizes and respects children's rights to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, freedom to express views, and participate in making decisions according to their capacity. 22. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in implementing social welfare efforts. 23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking as well as women and children victims of violence. 24. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and formed at the Regency, District and Village levels. Article 2

The principles of protection for Victims are:

a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; and
e. empowerment. Article 3

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children; b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence. Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling of victims of violence in the Region. CHAPTER II VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence against women and children include:

a. physical violence; b. psychological violence; c. sexual violence; d. domestic neglect; e. exploitation; and
f. other violence. Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury. Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of the household and/or outside the scope of the household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

CHAPTERV PROTECTION OF VICTIMS

Article 20

(1) Prevention efforts against violence against women and children are carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government coordinated by the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

(2) Prevention efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented by:

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns;
c. forming a violence prevention system; and
d. conducting socialization on laws and regulations related to the protection of women and child victims of violence.

Article 9

Domestic neglect as referred to in Article 5 letter d is:

a. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope whereas according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care or maintenance to that person.
b. the act of neglecting a person within the household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to him/her or due to an agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance to that person; and
c. an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

a. forming a work network in violence prevention efforts;

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

I. GENERAL

Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore it is necessary to protect their dignity and honor and guarantee their right to life in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in Southeast Minahasa Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and child victims of violence in the form of regional regulations.

Until now, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and child victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region, therefore institutional and regulatory support is needed to ensure its implementation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and child victims of violence in Southeast Minahasa Regency.

Regent is the Regent of Southeast Minahasa. 5. Provincial Government is the Provincial Government of North Sulawesi. 6. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional People's Representative Institution of Southeast Minahasa Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 7. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a Regional Government Work Unit related to the implementation of child protection. 8. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, hereinafter abbreviated as APBD, is the financial plan of the Region that is discussed and jointly approved by the Regional Government and DPRD and established by Regional Regulation. 9. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and/or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 11. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence, exploitation, discrimination, and neglect. 12. Special protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their development. 13. Parent is the biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother. 14. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward to the third degree. 16. Community is family, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Social Organization, hereinafter referred to as Orsos, is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community, whether legal entity or not, which functions as a means of community participation in implementing Social Welfare Efforts (UKS). 18. Child Protection Social House, hereinafter abbreviated as RSPA, is a child protection service unit for child victims of violence and child trafficking as a continuation of temporary shelter that functions to provide protection, recovery, rehabilitation, advocacy and referral. 19. Social Services for Children is physical, mental and social services aimed at helping children to grow and develop normally. 20. Social Services for Neglected Children is social services for children whose parents do not have the ability to meet the needs of children to grow and develop normally. 21. Child-friendly school is an educational institution that recognizes and respects children's rights to obtain education, health, opportunities to play and have fun, protection from violence and abuse, freedom to express views, and participate in making decisions according to their capacity. 22. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of knowledge, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in implementing social welfare efforts. 23. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of human trafficking as well as women and children victims of violence. 24. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for the prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is networked and formed at the Regency, District and Village levels. Article 2

The principles of protection for Victims are:

a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice and gender equality; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; and
e. empowerment. Article 3

The objectives of Victim Protection are:

a. to prevent violence against women and children; b. to provide services to Victims; and
c. to empower women victims of violence. Article 4

The scope of protection for victims includes prevention, service, empowerment and handling of victims of violence in the Region. CHAPTER II VIOLENCE

Article 5

Forms of violence against women and children include:

a. physical violence; b. psychological violence; c. sexual violence; d. domestic neglect; e. exploitation; and
f. other violence. Article 6

Physical violence as referred to in Article 5 letter a is that which results in pain, illness or serious injury. Article 7

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 5 letter b is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. Article 8

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 5 letter c includes:

a. forced sexual intercourse committed against a person residing within the scope of the household and/or outside the scope of the household; and
b. forced sexual intercourse against a person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

CHAPTER VII SUPERVISION AND MONITORING

Article 46

(1) The Regional Government conducts supervision and monitoring of the implementation of minimum service standards for every PPT in the Region.

(2) Supervision and Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. Monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, governance, funding, quality, control and monitoring.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c is carried out in accordance with laws and regulations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d is conducted periodically every 6 months.

CHAPTER VI INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER

Article 22

(1) PPT is established by the Regional Government in the form of a Technical Implementation Unit (UPT).

(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is a functional work unit that has the duties, main tasks, and functions of providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.

(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing temporary services and protection in the form of a safe house for victims of violence.

(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence are referred to a PPT that has a safe house.

(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) is established by Regional Regulation.

Article 23

(1) The organizational structure of PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 22 paragraph (1) consists of:

a. General Chairperson:
b. Secretary:
c. Treasurer; and
d. Executive Chairperson who oversees divisions.
(2) The divisions as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, at a minimum include:
a. complaint service division:
b. health service division:
c. social rehabilitation service division;
d. repatriation and social reintegration division; and
e. legal aid service division.
(3) In carrying out its duties, PPT is responsible to the Regent through the Head of the agency that has the main duties and functions of coordination in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
